clue.text: Scene of a towering row

parts.note: the biblical tower where builders were struck with mutually unintelligible tongues, so the 'row' is a din of languages at a tower, not a quarrel in a high place

explanation.walkthrough: 'Towering row' reads like a furious argument; it is literally a noisy confusion at a tower, from the Genesis story where speech was confounded.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genesis tower is where language was confused, making it the setting for a din of tongues at great height.

clue.text: Outline of a short play

explanation.definitionFit: A rough preliminary drawing gives an outline, and a brief comic scene in a revue is also so called.

clue.text: Example set by the ancients, maybe

indicators.note: letters that are set are arranged in a fresh order, so the word ancients is rearranged

explanation.surface: A precedent laid down long ago by the people of antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like part of 'set an example' but signals rearranging the letters of ANCIENTS; 'maybe' marks the definition as one sense among others.
explanation.definitionFit: A case in point is a specimen or illustration, which is what an example is.

clue.text: Jettison a substandard cargo

parts.note: food that has gone off is below standard
a load is the goods carried by a vessel or lorry

explanation.surface: A ship throws overboard a poor-quality shipment.
explanation.definitionFit: To unload or dump something unwanted is to get rid of it, as jettisoning does.

clue.text: Whacked a loafer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Whacked' is British slang for exhausted, not struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Two words, it means utterly exhausted, like 'whacked'; one word, it is an idle layabout who shirks work or debts.

clue.text: He takes note

parts.note: reads like someone paying attention, but means a courier carrying a written note to its recipient

explanation.definitionFit: A courier carries letters and notes from one person to another.

clue.text: Kind of dive lorry drivers try to avoid

explanation.walkthrough: An articulated lorry that folds so the trailer swings round against the cab is said to do this.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive in which the body bends double before straightening shares its name with the folding skid of an articulated truck.

clue.text: A column seen in flight

parts.note: a flight here is a flight of stairs, and the column is the central post at its foot or around which a spiral staircase winds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests aircraft or birds; it is a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright post supporting a staircase handrail or forming the core of a winding stair is this architectural term.

clue.text: One who studies hard and pulls up

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to pull a vehicle along behind is to tow it

explanation.surface: A diligent student who also does weight-training pull-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TOWS round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a pupil who works obsessively at books, a grind.

clue.text: What the driver needs on the whole is to be sober

parts.note: a golfer's driver needs a tee to hit the ball off
the total is the whole amount

explanation.surface: Advice that a motorist should, all things considered, stay off the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'driver' is a golf club, not a motorist; a golfer tees the ball up before using it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains completely from alcohol is always sober.

clue.text: We'd sit out, in the broadest sense

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the words before it are put out of order

explanation.surface: We'd stay seated outside, speaking in very general terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatest in width is a superlative meaning most wide.

clue.text: It's just a question of time

definitions.text: It's just a question of time

parts.words: It's just a question of time
parts.note: the idiom for something inevitable, read literally as a word that asks only about time

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means 'inevitable'; read literally it describes an interrogative word asking at what time.
explanation.definitionFit: This interrogative asks at what time something happens.

clue.text: He comes in to wait, finally

indicators.note: comes in says the word he enters the middle of the other piece

parts.note: to wait on or serve someone is to attend them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man arrives to serve as a waiter, at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-word phrase meaning in the end or eventually, which is what finally means.

clue.text: Soldier to offer information unasked

explanation.definitionFit: An enlisted person who signs up freely is one sort of soldier, and to come forward with facts without being asked is the verb sense.

clue.text: The widow who urges one to take a gamble

definitions.text: who urges one to take a gamble

explanation.walkthrough: Split two and five, the second sense reads as an imperative telling someone to place a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A titled widow holding property from her late husband is a dowager; split, 'do wager' urges someone to bet.

clue.text: Order a dessert

explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple-pie order' is an idiom for perfect neatness.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect neatness is called apple-pie order, and the fruit-filled pastry is a familiar pudding.

clue.text: Book that's dull gets cut

parts.note: a matt finish is dull, not glossy
to hew is to chop or cut

explanation.surface: A boring volume is edited down.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Gospel of the New Testament is one of the books of the Bible.

clue.text: Dutch barrister's liqueur

explanation.walkthrough: The liqueur's name is the Dutch word for a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: The egg-and-brandy drink takes its name from the Dutch word for an advocate or lawyer.

clue.text: Sister diverted with love romances

indicators.note: diverted means turned aside from its course, so these letters are sent into a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A nun is distracted by thoughts of affection and love affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tales of love or adventure are narratives, the plural noun sense of romances.

clue.text: As worn by a parachutist?

parts.note: describes a one-piece garment, playing on the idea of an outfit suited to someone who leaps out of aircraft

explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece overall originally made for skydivers covering body, arms and legs.

clue.text: Vessels of the royal navy in America

indicators.note: in places the navy's abbreviation inside the abbreviation for America

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States
RN is the abbreviation for the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: British warships stationed in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests ships, matching the navy; it means containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Vases or containers, often for ashes, are vessels in the sense of receptacles.

clue.text: Carve a large slice of meat

indicators.note: a slice of these words is a run cut out of them

explanation.surface: Instructions to carve a big piece of roast.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'carVE A Large'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calf flesh is a kind of meat.

clue.text: Get off with a blonde

parts.note: light hair is fair or blonde

explanation.surface: Making a pass at a fair-haired woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get off with' suggests a romantic conquest; 'get off' alone means dismount.
explanation.definitionFit: To step down from a bus or horse is to dismount.

clue.text: Set out pictures on the street

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
art means paintings and pictures

explanation.surface: Arranging paintings for display along the pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin a journey is to depart or begin.

clue.text: Scattered the rest around two points of the compass

indicators.note: around shows the letters of rest moved round into a new order

parts.note: W and N stand for west and north

explanation.surface: The remainder was strewn widely in two directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges REST to STRE, followed by W and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Things spread untidily over an area are distributed loosely, the past participle sense.

clue.text: I respect new evidence of settlements

indicators.note: new tells us to make a new arrangement of the letters of I respect

explanation.surface: A person admits respect for fresh proof of deals.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofs of payment show that bills have been paid.

clue.text: Soldier in ebbing sea gets protection

indicators.note: in places the soldier inside the turned-round sea
an ebbing tide flows back, so the word sea runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written
GI is an American enlisted soldier

explanation.surface: An infantryman stranded in a retreating tide finds shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ebbing' turns SEA into AES, and 'in' puts GI inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Under someone's auspices or patronage means under their protection.

clue.text: These, when mixed, harm poets

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of harm poets are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Muddled figures of speech grate on writers of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when mixed' doubles as the familiar 'mixed metaphor', so the whole clue reads as a comment on clumsy imagery.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures of speech describing one thing as another are the subject 'These' points to.
